text:
maria: Ran a 2h probe of the continuous-batcher with a new micro-bucketizer for prompt lengths + decode rate stratification. Putting notes here, need quick sanity check before I run a longer sweep.

liam: Nice — what buckets did you use?

maria: length buckets: [0-16,17-64,65-256,257+] (heuristic derived from p50/p90 length hist). decode-rate buckets: slow (<20 tok/s), mid (20-80 tok/s), fast (>80 tok/s). Token-budget target per bucket: {0-16:64,17-64:256,65-256:768,257+:1024}.

zoe: Quick question: how are you measuring decode-rate? wall-clock on first 128 tokens or model-reported?

maria: model-reported decode throughput averaged over first 32 tokens for each request, then smoothed with EWMA(0.2). That avoids startup jitter.

liam: EWMA makes sense. Any surprises in the KV cache interaction?

maria: Yes — small but reproducible perf regression on mixed workloads when micro-buckets are tiny (0-16) and token_budget is low. Prefetch probe shows KV cache thrash for cohorts that oscillate between fast/mid decode-rate.

perf-bot: Profiling snapshot 1976543240:
```
sample: 30s window
p50 latency: 28ms
p95 latency: 140ms (up from 120ms baseline)
decode tokens/s (avg): 62
kv-lookup QPS: +22% vs baseline
batch size mean: 6 -> 4 when oscillation present
```

maria: Repro script (local):
```
# quick runner
./run_probe --workload mix.json --bucketizer micro --buckets "[16,64,256]" --token-budgets "[64,256,768,1024]" --decay 0.2
```

zoe: Could the regression be kernel-selection churn? If batches shrink, different matmul kernel chosen which is slower for small batch sizes. We saw that last quarter.

liam: Good point. Check kernel flip counts in the trace (kernel_switch metric). If >5% flips under these oscillation patterns that's your culprit.

maria: I pulled kernel_switch: 8.6% in mixed run. Also saw increased memcpy work in KV prefetch path. So two factors: kernel selection thrash + KV prefetch causing IO bursts.

zoe: Options: 1) widen micro-buckets to reduce flip frequency, 2) add hysteresis to token-budget changes, 3) limit KV prefetch concurrency for small buckets.

liam: I'd try hysteresis first (only change bucket when EWMA crosses threshold by 15%). That avoids oscillation between mid/fast. Also add a small grace period (200ms) before shrinking a batch.

maria: I'll implement EWMA threshold + 200ms grace. Also run a run with kernel pinning for critical small-batch kernels to confirm impact. Plan: 1h run today with hysteresis, 1h run tomorrow with kernel pin pinned.

perf-bot: Added perf job 1976543260 -> queued. Notifying when finished. :rocket:

liam: Thx. If pinning fixes p95, we should consider a kernel-selection cooldown in runtime rather than pinning permanently.

maria: Agreed. I'll paste results when the job completes. For the long sweep I'll also record per-request bucket transitions so we can quantify oscillation rates.

zoe: Nice. One more ask: add a small eval set with long prompt but fast decode (e.g., 1024 tokens from batched retrieval) to ensure large-bucket latencies don't regress with new token-budget targets.

maria: Will do. Thanks all.

liam: :thumbsup:
